comparisons.peer_topic: On-Premises Edge AI and Computing Platforms
comparisons.peer_summary: The company develops high-performance, AI-enabled compute platforms using Intel Xeon, Core, and Atom processors for industries like retail and healthcare, delivering edge-optimized platforms to reduce operational complexity and enable faster data processing at the edge.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Intel focus on extending AI capabilities into edge and embedded systems, though they target different hardware architectures. AMD describes its strategy around launching Versal Series Gen 2 adaptive SoCs that integrate preprocessing, AI inference, and postprocessing for 'end-to-end acceleration of AI-driven embedded systems.' In contrast, Intel focuses on delivering 'edge-optimized AI-enabled platforms' based on its Xeon, Core, and Atom processor portfolios to help customers 'create, store, and process data at the edge' for industries like retail and healthcare. While both aim to accelerate AI at the edge, AMD emphasizes adaptive compute solutions for embedded integration, whereas Intel highlights broader multi-architecture platforms for general edge industries.

sentences.text: We expanded our adaptive computing portfolio with differentiated solutions with the launch of the new Versal™ Series Gen 2 devices, including the new Versal AI Edge Series Gen 2 and Versal Prime Series Gen 2 adaptive SoCs, which bring preprocessing, AI inference, and postprocessing together in a single device for end-to-end acceleration of AI-driven embedded systems.

We deliver edge-optimized AI-enabled platforms for edge applications based on our Intel Xeon, Intel Core, and Intel Atom® processor portfolio, which reduces operational complexity for our customers and helps our customers create, store, and process data at the edge so they can analyze it faster and act on it sooner.

We develop high-performance, AI-enabled compute platforms that solve for technology and business use cases that scale across several industries, such as retail, education, manufacturing, energy, healthcare, and medical.

comparisons.peer_topic: Client Compute Brand Strategy and Product Portfolio
comparisons.peer_summary: In 2023, Intel updated its client compute brands to Intel, Intel Core, and Intel Core Ultra, with Intel Core representing highest volume in 2024. The Intel Core Ultra family, launched late 2023, introduced the AI PC with advancements in graphics, AI, and CPU performance, followed by the next-generation Intel Core Ultra 200V Series in H2 2024 for mobile PCs and the Intel Core Ultra 200S Series for desktop enthusiasts.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies are driving portfolio expansions centered on AI performance in mobile and client computing, but AMD targets the embedded/adaptive sector while Intel targets the consumer client market. AMD expanded its adaptive computing portfolio with Versal devices for 'AI-driven embedded systems,' focusing on specialized pre- and post-processing acceleration. Intel updated its client brands with the 'Intel Core Ultra' family, which 'introduced the AI PC to the market' with advancements in graphics and AI for mobile PCs. Both disclosures highlight a strategic shift toward integrating AI acceleration directly into their respective processor families (Versal for AMD, Core Ultra for Intel) to address growing AI workloads.

sentences.text: We expanded our adaptive computing portfolio with differentiated solutions with the launch of the new Versal™ Series Gen 2 devices, including the new Versal AI Edge Series Gen 2 and Versal Prime Series Gen 2 adaptive SoCs, which bring preprocessing, AI inference, and postprocessing together in a single device for end-to-end acceleration of AI-driven embedded systems.

The Intel Core Ultra processor family, which we launched at the end of 2023, delivers significant advancements in graphics, AI, and multi-threaded CPU performance and introduced the AI PC to the market.
In the second half of 2024, the next-generation Intel Core Ultra 200V Series became our highest performance client processors, with increased battery life for mobile PCs.
